decision: Execute the selected current-Nanoda literal-test repair as the sole ACTIVE item after committing its exact source lock, non-vacuity rubric and finite process limits. Its source-established test-effectiveness defect and short path to a maintainable external patch outrank the still-feasible corpus, cache, contract and discovery alternatives for this one-item run.

categories.assessment: The portfolio keeps checker hardening, shared corpus work, implementation-independent contract clarification and bounded history mining available. A focused test-effectiveness repair is the smallest decisive implementation item; no new method or mutation campaign is introduced.

The selected item can turn a concrete ineffective assertion into executable non-vacuity coverage for an upstream checker. Arena let reuse and the inference-cache regression remain the strongest shared-asset alternatives but require broader policy or fixture work.

Current Nanoda source and tests are already bound, the distinct zero-thread PR is known and must not be duplicated, and no newer maintainer trigger outranks this small test-only repair. Submission remains outside authority.

No new theory is needed for the finite Option-returning test premise. The completed source review and current primary source are sufficient; semantic contract items retain their own primary-source budgets and the HSBM review is current.

All nine executable candidates have local entry paths. The selected repair has the fewest unresolved semantic and fixture dependencies, while its exact detached checkout, locked dependencies and finite test matrix make it immediately falsifiable.

candidates.rationale: The exact current source predicts a None-only test, the action rubric makes reproduction and repair falsifiable, and the detached source plus locked test commands fit the remaining budget.
Existing exact bytes make the corpus audit executable, but duplicate and expected-outcome qualification give it a longer path than the selected checker test repair.
The internal staged-cache witness is durable and the item is executable, but current pointer-lifetime fixture work is less direct than repairing the already identified literal test.
The focused source review is locally executable and valuable for shared outcome language, but it is less likely to yield an immediate executable asset than the selected patch.
The six-commit pilot is bounded and its methods review is current, but discovery follows cheaper concrete contribution candidates in the authorized portfolio.
The source-only negative-cache audit is independently executable, but it currently offers a protocol decision rather than a validated patch and remains lower ranked.
The bounded current-corpus audit remains executable, but selecting a useful isolation improvement requires more case and outcome analysis than this exact test repair.
The grouped import-contract clarification is useful and locally executable, but its broader field scope makes it less decisive than the selected finite implementation test.
The reserved-namespace audit is a valid independent reserve, but it still needs exact attribution and an input/control design while the literal-test gap is already source-established.
